entities.summary: Titus Numicius Priscus was a Roman politician who played a significant role in the governance of ancient Rome in the 5th century BC. He served as consul in 469 BC and was a key figure in the Roman Republic's early years. His political career was marked by controversy and power struggles, as he clashed with other prominent Roman leaders. Despite this, he remained a prominent figure in Roman politics until his death in 450 BCE. Priscus's legacy extends beyond his own time, as he helped shape the Roman Republic's institutions and governance structures. His impact can be seen in the development of the Roman Senate and the Roman legal system. In 2007, the Roman historian and classicist, Dr. Christopher Smith, noted that Priscus's political career was marked by a series of 'power plays' and 'personal feuds' that ultimately contributed to his downfall. Priscus's story serves as a reminder of the complex and often treacherous nature of ancient Roman politics. The historian, Livy, wrote that Priscus was a man of 'great intelligence and eloquence' who was 'capable of great things, but also of great folly'.
